description: Multi-mode filter running one of twelve responses at a time, polyphonic to 16 voices, with a saturating drive stage ahead of the filter

params.text: Sets the filter corner, 20Hz at the left and 20kHz at the right
Sets the resonance at the corner, sweeping the filter damping from 0.707 at the left to 0.01 at the right
Sets the gain into a soft-clipping stage ahead of the filter, unity at the left and ten times at the right
Scales the Cutoff CV input before it shifts the corner, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales the Reso CV input before it changes the damping, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales the Drive CV input before it is added to the drive, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned

inputs.text: The signal to be filtered; its channel count sets how many voices the module runs, and it is divided by 5 on the way in and multiplied by 5 again at the output
Multiplies the corner by two raised to its own voltage, after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 20Hz and 20kHz
Raises the resonance after the attenuverter beside it, each volt at a full attenuverter taking 0.2 off the damping, and the damping is held between 0.01 and 0.707
Adds a tenth of its voltage to the drive after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1

outputs.text: The filtered signal, carrying one channel per voice of the input

notes: the response is picked on the mode display rather than by a knob: a left click steps to the next of the twelve and a right click opens a menu of them.
the mode display is drawn rather than being a parameter, so clicking it never reaches a help line.
the twelve responses are LP 6dB, LP 12dB, LP 24dB, HP 6dB, HP 12dB, HP 24dB, BP, BP+, Notch, Notch+, AP and AP+.
the four responses marked with a plus run two identical two-pole sections in series, doubling the slope of the plain one, and Reso has no effect on the two 6dB responses, which are one-pole.
changing the response clears the filter state on every voice, so a note sounding at the time restarts rather than crossfades.
a mono cable, or one with fewer channels than the input, is copied to every voice on each of the three CV jacks.
this module is kept so that patches already using it keep loading, and it is hidden from the module browser. VortexV2 is the current one.
menu: Filter Mode — on the mode display rather than the panel: lists the twelve responses and sets the one in use
